claims.text: High configurational entropy favors chemically disordered solid-solution phases in equiatomic multi-metal alloys.
Increasing temperature strengthens configurational-entropy stabilization by lowering the relative free energy of simple solid solutions and making ordered intermetallic phases less competitive.
Favorable enthalpic interactions can overcome configurational entropy and drive chemical ordering.
Atomic-size mismatch produces lattice distortion that promotes short-range chemical ordering.
Substantial lattice distortion raises atomic-diffusion barriers and thereby produces sluggish diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion suppresses the atomic rearrangements required for ordering or phase separation.
Across 473–1923 K, thermal energy and distortion-induced kinetic barriers together allow configurational entropy to dominate when atomic-size mismatch is moderate.
If atomic-size mismatch exceeds a critical threshold, local enthalpic attractions overcome kinetic suppression and trigger chemical ordering or segregation.
Rapid thermal-shock synthesis can produce single-phase, homogeneous multi-metal nanoparticles with random atomic distributions.
Several hours per thermal cycle are sufficient to permit diagnostically relevant atomic diffusion over 473–1923 K.
An inert or controlled atmosphere prevents oxidation from affecting the thermal-stability comparison.
Nanoparticles with moderate atomic-size mismatch will retain a homogeneous solid solution with minimal ordering or segregation throughout thermal cycling from 473 to 1923 K.
Nanoparticles with larger atomic-size mismatch will develop more detectable short-range order or incipient phase separation than the moderate-mismatch particles under the same thermal conditions.
The stability prediction applies only when atomic-size differences remain below an ordering threshold and exposure times remain shorter than those required for complete equilibration.
Significant ordering or phase separation in the minimal-distortion set would falsify the proposed entropy-plus-distortion mechanism.

contradictions.description: The design says the two nanoparticle sets have identical overall composition while also saying different constituent elements are chosen to alter atomic-radius dispersion. Changing elemental identities changes composition, so both conditions cannot hold simultaneously.

The prediction identifies moderate mismatch as the stable regime, whereas the falsification rule treats minimal mismatch as the expected stable regime. These are not necessarily the same comparison group, making the stated falsification criterion misaligned with the primary prediction.
